findings.title: Shard-split queries are interpolated twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables for every target, and the resulting sub-requests are then passed to runSplitQuery, which at querySplitting.ts:299 calls applyTemplateVariables again for the same targets (the updated shard test even expects 5 calls for 1 initial query plus 4 shard sub-requests). Loki's applyTemplateVariables is not guaranteed idempotent: it applies request.filters/ad-hoc filters to the expression in addition to replacing variables, so a second pass can append the same ad-hoc label/filter twice, and any variable value containing a '$'-expression can be re-expanded. Shard splitting should interpolate only once, either here or in runSplitQuery, not both.

findings.title: Queries that interpolate to an empty expression are no longer dropped
findings.body: The empty check runs on the raw expression before interpolation: .filter((query) => query.expr).map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(...)), with no re-filter afterwards (the same ordering is used in shardQuerySplitting.ts:49-52). A target whose expression is only a template variable, e.g. expr: '$expr', passes the raw check but can interpolate to '' when the variable has no value; it is then classified by isLogsQuery/querySupportsSplitting, grouped, and sent to Loki as an empty query instead of being skipped like a directly-empty query, producing backend parse errors for the whole panel request. Filter again after applyTemplateVariables (or interpolate first, then filter).
